meta.rule: Records who can actually direct the company, not who holds the most shares. Passive index managers are never recorded as controllers; where nobody controls the company, that is stated as the finding.

parent.label: Subsidiary
parent.meaning: Majority- or wholly-owned by another company, which decides.

state.label: State-controlled
state.meaning: A government, sovereign fund or state investment vehicle holds control or a decisive bloc.

founder.label: Founder or family controlled
founder.meaning: A founder, family or their holding vehicles exercise control, whether or not they hold a majority of the economics.

dual_class.label: Dual-class voting control
dual_class.meaning: Voting power is detached from economic ownership by a special share class, so a small economic stake controls the company.

foundation.label: Foundation-controlled
foundation.meaning: A charitable or industrial foundation holds the capital, with voting exercised separately.

consortium.label: Consortium-controlled
consortium.meaning: Control is held jointly by a defined group of investors under an agreement.

strategic.label: Strategic blockholder
strategic.meaning: A corporate holder with a large, non-passive stake short of a majority — influential, and not a custodian.

partnership.label: Partnership board control
partnership.meaning: A defined partnership body nominates a majority of the board regardless of shareholding.

institute.label: Public research institute
institute.meaning: Not an investor-owned company: a public or non-profit research organisation.

division.label: Division, not a company
division.meaning: Not a separate legal entity in its own right — a unit of its parent.

widely_held.label: No controller — widely held
widely_held.meaning: No shareholder controls it. The largest holders are passive index managers, which are custodians of other people's money, not directors of the business.

unestablished.label: Control not established here
unestablished.meaning: This dataset could not establish control from a public source it was willing to cite.

limits: Control is a point-in-time fact and the most perishable data in this project. Stakes move, consortia sell down, and a company that was state-controlled last year may not be this year.

A percentage is recorded only where control genuinely runs through one. Founder, foundation, partnership and dual-class control often do not, and a missing percentage there is correct rather than absent.
‘Widely held’ is a positive finding, not a gap: it means no shareholder controls the company. It does not mean the research was not done.
Entries at evidence tier D are flagged low confidence. They name a mechanism this dataset believes is real without a filing it was willing to cite for the current holder.
This dataset feeds no score, no index and no propagation. It is reference material.

arm.basis: SoftBank retained the large majority of Arm after the September 2023 IPO floated a small minority.

imec.controller: imec (an independent non-profit research institute, Flanders)
imec.basis: A Flemish public research institute funded by government and an industry affiliate programme — it has no controlling shareholder because it has no shareholders in the ordinary sense.

synopsys.basis: No controlling shareholder. The largest holders are passive index managers.

cadence.basis: No controlling shareholder. The largest holders are passive index managers.

siemens_eda.basis: Siemens EDA is the former Mentor Graphics, operating inside Siemens Digital Industries Software. It is a business unit, not an independent company.

nvidia.basis: No controlling shareholder. The founder-CEO holds a low single-digit stake, which is influence, not control.

amd.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are passive index managers.

qualcomm.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are passive index managers.

apple.basis: No controlling shareholder. Berkshire Hathaway's position is large in money terms and small in percentage, and is not a control stake.

mediatek.basis: No controlling shareholder; founders retain influence through board representation rather than a控制 bloc.
mediatek.note: Founder influence is real but not expressible as a control stake, so it is not recorded as one.

hisilicon.basis: A wholly-owned fabless design subsidiary of Huawei. The U.S. Entity List rule of August 2020 names it among Huawei's affiliates.

shinetsu.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are institutions and nominee trusts.

sumco.basis: No controlling shareholder. Its founding parents, Sumitomo Metal Industries and Mitsubishi Materials, reduced their stakes after listing.

globalwafers.basis: GlobalWafers was spun out of SAS, which retains roughly half the shares and board control.

jsr.controller: Japan Investment Corporation (JIC), a government-backed fund
jsr.basis: JIC's vehicle JICC-02 completed a tender offer for about 84% of JSR in April 2024, taking it private. An explicitly industrial-policy acquisition of a photoresist leader.

tok.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are institutions and nominee trusts.

linde.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are passive index managers.

airliquide.basis: No controlling shareholder; a notably dispersed register including a large retail shareholder base.

ibiden.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are institutions and nominee trusts.

unimicron.basis: Unimicron was founded out of the UMC group, whose affiliates remain among the largest identified holders.
unimicron.note: The current aggregate affiliate holding is not clearly disclosed; recorded as a strategic bloc rather than control.

asml.basis: No controlling shareholder. Dutch law and ASML's own structure leave no blockholder; its export exposure is to state policy, not state ownership.

nikon.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are institutions and nominee trusts.

canon.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are institutions and nominee trusts.

amat.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are passive index managers.

tel.basis: No controlling shareholder. Its two largest lines are Japanese nominee trust banks, which are custodial accounts rather than beneficial owners.

lam.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are passive index managers.

kla.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are passive index managers.

tsmc.basis: No controlling shareholder. Taiwan's National Development Fund is the largest single holder at roughly 6.4% — a government anchor stake that does not amount to control.

samsung.controller: the Lee family, through Samsung Group affiliate cross-holdings
samsung.basis: Control runs through a web of affiliate holdings (notably Samsung Life and Samsung C&T) rather than a direct majority.

intel.basis: No controlling shareholder. The U.S. government took roughly 9.9% in 2025 by converting CHIPS Act funding into common equity — the largest single holder, and still not control.

rapidus.controller: the Japanese government (NEDO) with a 32-company industrial consortium
rapidus.basis: Built as a national project: state funding with a golden-share arrangement alongside Toyota, Sony, SoftBank, Kioxia, NTT, NEC, MUFG and others.

smic.controller: Chinese state investment vehicles acting together (China IC Big Fund, Datang Telecom, Shanghai IC Fund)
smic.basis: SMIC discloses no single controlling shareholder; its largest holders are state vehicles whose combined bloc is decisive.
smic.note: Recorded as state-controlled on the combined bloc, with the no-single-controller disclosure stated alongside.

umc.basis: No controlling shareholder; a dispersed register typical of older Taiwanese listings.

gf.controller: Mubadala Investment Company (Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund)
gf.basis: Mubadala has been GlobalFoundries' majority owner since before the 2021 IPO and remains so after it.

ti.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are passive index managers.

infineon.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are passive index managers.

st.controller: the French and Italian governments jointly, through ST Holding N.V.
st.basis: A shareholders' agreement between the two states gives joint control of roughly 27.5% of the capital. One of the few chip firms under explicit dual-state control.

tower.basis: No controlling shareholder. Intel's agreed acquisition was abandoned in 2023, leaving Tower independent and dispersed.

skhynix.controller: SK Square, within the SK Group (Chey family)
skhynix.basis: SK Square holds about 20.5%, which is the controlling bloc inside Korea's chaebol holding structure.

micron.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are passive index managers.

ymtc.controller: Hubei provincial state vehicles with the China IC Big Fund
ymtc.basis: Yangtze Memory is a provincial-state project, funded through Hubei development vehicles and the national fund.

cxmt.basis: ChangXin Memory was built as a Hefei municipal project and remains state-anchored.

kioxia.controller: a Bain Capital-led consortium, with Toshiba as the second holder
kioxia.basis: Bain retained roughly half and Toshiba roughly a third after the December 2024 IPO; SK hynix is reported as the third-largest holder.
kioxia.note: Reported post-IPO percentages differ between sources, and one report of a full Bain exit could not be confirmed. Treat the figure as approximate.

ase.controller: the Chang family (founder Jason Chang and affiliates)
ase.basis: ASE Technology Holding is founder-controlled through family and affiliate holdings rather than a single majority line.

amkor.controller: the Kim family (founder James Kim and family trusts)
amkor.basis: The founding family holds about half the shares, which is outright control of a listed OSAT.

jcet.controller: the China IC Big Fund and state-linked holders
jcet.basis: The national fund has been JCET's largest shareholder; the disclosed controller has changed with successive transfers between state-linked vehicles.
jcet.note: Flagged low confidence: the controlling entity has moved more than once and the current disclosure was not verified here.

foxconn.basis: No controlling shareholder any longer. The founder's family stake has fallen to mid-single digits, and family holding companies disclosed disposing of their remaining Hon Hai shares in December 2025.
foxconn.note: Foxconn is widely read as founder-controlled; on the current register it is not.

ibm_res.basis: IBM Research is a division of IBM, not a separate company. It has no ownership of its own.

leti.controller: CEA (French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission)
leti.basis: CEA-Leti is an institute of the CEA, a French state research body.

ansys.basis: Synopsys completed its acquisition of Ansys in 2025; Ansys no longer reports independently.

empyrean.basis: Empyrean's disclosed controlling chain runs to CEC, a centrally administered state-owned enterprise.
empyrean.note: The intermediate holding entities have changed with successive restructurings; the state root is the stable part.

broadcom.basis: No controlling shareholder. Leadership influence is strong and is not an ownership stake.

marvell.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are passive index managers.

unisoc.controller: the post-restructuring Tsinghua Unigroup consortium (JAC Capital / Wise Road Capital)
unisoc.basis: UNISOC sits under Tsinghua Unigroup, whose 2022 court-supervised restructuring transferred control to an investor consortium.
unisoc.note: The consortium's internal split is not fully public; the fact of consortium control is.

sksiltron.basis: SK Inc. holds a controlling stake; SK Siltron is a member company of the SK chaebol.

siltronic.basis: Wacker holds roughly 30.8% — short of a majority, but the decisive bloc, and Siltronic was carved out of Wacker.

nsig.controller: Shanghai state investment vehicles with the China National IC Industry Investment Fund
nsig.basis: National Silicon Industry Group is a Shanghai state-sponsored consolidation of China's wafer industry.

sumitomo_chem.basis: No controlling shareholder. Sumitomo group affiliation is a keiretsu relationship, not a control stake.

dupont.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are passive index managers.

resonac.basis: No controlling shareholder. Formerly Showa Denko.

tnsc.basis: Nippon Sanso Holdings, the parent of Taiyo Nippon Sanso, is majority-held by Mitsubishi Chemical Group.

airproducts.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are passive index managers.

skmaterials.basis: SK Materials was merged into SK Inc. in 2021 and operates as part of the SK group's materials arm.

shinko.controller: a Japan Investment Corporation-led consortium (JIC 80%, Dai Nippon Printing 15%, Mitsui Chemicals 5%)
shinko.basis: Acquired from Fujitsu by the JIC-led consortium; the tender offer completed and the company delisted in 2025.

samsungem.controller: Samsung Electronics and the wider Samsung Group (Lee family)
samsungem.basis: Samsung Electronics holds roughly 23.7% of Samsung Electro-Mechanics, inside the Lee family's group structure.

ats.controller: the Androsch and Dörflinger private foundations, acting under a syndicate agreement
ats.basis: Two Austrian private foundations hold roughly 40% jointly and syndicate their votes.
ats.note: The model files AT&S under Germany; the company is Austrian.

asmi.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are passive index managers.

kokusai.basis: KKR bought Kokusai Electric from Hitachi, listed it in 2023 and has been selling down a large residual stake.
kokusai.note: The residual percentage moves with each sell-down, so no figure is recorded.

naura.controller: Beijing Electronics Holding (a Beijing municipal state-owned enterprise)
naura.basis: NAURA's disclosed actual controller chain runs to the Beijing municipal state assets administration.

amec.basis: AMEC states in its own A-share disclosure that it has NO controlling shareholder and NO actual controller (无实际控制人) — an unusual and deliberate structure for a Chinese equipment maker.

hitachiht.basis: Hitachi High-Tech was taken fully private by Hitachi in 2020 and is a wholly-owned subsidiary.

ebara.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are institutions and nominee trusts.

entegris.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are passive index managers.

onto.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are passive index managers.

nova.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are passive index managers.

huahong.controller: Shanghai Hua Hong (Group), a Shanghai state-owned enterprise
huahong.basis: Hua Hong Semiconductor's controlling chain runs to the Shanghai state assets administration.

vis.basis: TSMC holds roughly 28% of Vanguard International Semiconductor, its largest shareholder, and the two have a long-standing operational relationship.

nexchip.basis: Nexchip was established as a Hefei municipal joint venture and remains state-anchored.

sonysemi.basis: Sony Semiconductor Solutions is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Sony Group.

renesas.basis: No controlling shareholder following the INCJ sell-down. Denso and Toyota retain strategic stakes well short of control.
renesas.note: Control here moved materially over the last decade; the current state is dispersed.

bosch.controller: Robert Bosch Stiftung, with voting exercised by Robert Bosch Industrietreuhand KG
bosch.basis: The foundation holds about 92% of the capital while the voting rights sit with an industrial trust — capital and control deliberately separated, and the reason Bosch answers to no public market.

nanya.basis: Nanya Technology is a Formosa Plastics group company; group entities hold the decisive bloc.

winbond.controller: the Jiao family through Walsin Lihwa and affiliates
winbond.basis: Winbond sits inside the Walsin group, controlled by the founding family.

google.controller: Larry Page and Sergey Brin, through Class B super-voting shares
google.basis: The founders hold roughly a majority of voting power on a far smaller economic stake — the textbook case of votes detached from ownership.

amazon.basis: No controlling shareholder. The founder remains the largest individual holder at under a tenth, which is influence rather than control.

cambricon.basis: Disclosed in its A-share filings as the actual controller (实际控制人).

biren.basis: A private, venture-funded company. Its shareholder register is not public in enough detail to name a controller.
biren.note: Named here as unestablished rather than guessed.

onsemi.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are passive index managers.

adi.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are passive index managers.

nxp.basis: No controlling shareholder. The private-equity consortium that once owned it exited long ago.

microchip.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are passive index managers.

spil.basis: SPIL has been a wholly-owned ASE subsidiary since 2018; its output is consolidated into ASE's accounts.

pti.controller: the founding management group (D.K. Tsai and affiliates)
pti.basis: Powertech is founder-led with management and affiliate holdings forming the largest bloc.
pti.note: Flagged low confidence: no single disclosed controlling shareholder was verified here.

utac.basis: UTAC Holdings was acquired by Wise Road Capital in 2020 and is privately held by it.

kyec.basis: No controlling shareholder identified; a dispersed Taiwanese register.
kyec.note: Flagged low confidence: dispersed registers are easy to mistake for an absence of research.

inari.basis: Insas Berhad holds roughly a fifth of Inari Amertron and is its anchor shareholder.

quanta.controller: Barry Lam (co-founder and chairman) with affiliated holdings
quanta.basis: Founder-led, with the chairman's holdings forming the largest identified bloc.

wistron.basis: Spun out of Acer and run by its founding management; no single majority holder.
wistron.note: Flagged low confidence: recorded as founder-led influence rather than verified control.

supermicro.controller: Charles Liang (co-founder and CEO) with family holdings
supermicro.basis: The founder-CEO holds the largest single block, well short of a majority but decisive in practice.

luxshare.controller: Wang Laichun and Wang Laisheng, through Luxshare Limited
luxshare.basis: Disclosed in Luxshare's A-share filings as the actual controllers (实际控制人).

microsoft.basis: No controlling shareholder. A former CEO is the largest individual holder at a few percent.

meta.controller: Mark Zuckerberg, through Class B super-voting shares
meta.basis: Roughly 61% of voting power on an economic stake near 13%.

alibaba.basis: The Partnership has the right to nominate a majority of the board, so board control does not follow shareholding. SoftBank and Altaba were historically the largest holders without controlling it.

tesla.basis: The founder-CEO is by far the largest individual holder and exercises decisive influence without a majority.

denso.controller: the Toyota Group (Toyota Motor and Toyota Industries)
denso.basis: Toyota Motor holds roughly a quarter and Toyota Industries a further slice; Denso is a core Toyota group supplier.

vw.controller: Porsche SE (the Porsche and Piëch families), with the State of Lower Saxony holding a statutory blocking minority
vw.basis: Porsche SE holds about 53% of voting rights; the VW Law gives Lower Saxony's ~20% a blocking power no ordinary 20% would carry. Family control and state veto in the same company.

xiaomi.controller: Lei Jun (founder), through weighted voting rights
xiaomi.basis: Xiaomi's dual-class structure under the Hong Kong WVR regime gives the founder voting control on a minority economic stake.

lenovo.controller: Legend Holdings, in which the Chinese Academy of Sciences holds an indirect stake
lenovo.basis: Legend Holdings is the largest shareholder; the state connection is indirect, through Legend rather than through Lenovo.

hp.basis: No controlling shareholder; largest holders are passive index managers.
